title: Session Chronicle: unified query panels for trace pivoting and request drill-down
creator: Noah Chen
description:
Problem: Operators and engineers need a faster way to pivot from a high-level latency/cost spike into the sequence-level request detail (spans, correlation IDs, timeline) without context-switching across multiple panels. Current trace flows are fragmented: filter UIs live separately from timeline and span detail drawers, which makes correlation searches (by correlation ID, request hash, or session) slow and error-prone.

Goal: Design a single 'Session Chronicle' UX pattern that exposes: a unified query panel (filters + search + saved queries), an integrated timeline with span stacking, and a detachable request detail canvas that surfaces correlation IDs, raw payloads, and related requests. The pattern should support fast pivoting (keyboard + click targets), retained query state across navigation, and clear copy for security and data retention constraints.

Scope: This ticket covers the interaction model, high-fidelity screen designs for desktop, micro-interaction prototypes (keyboard-driven pivoting, inline search-as-you-type, timeline scrub), accessibility considerations, and a set of handoff assets for frontend and backend teams (API contract sketches, telemetry events). Backend implementation and API contracts are tracked in ENG-43210 (dependencies).

Success metrics: reduce mean time-to-investigate (MTTI) for tracing incidents by 30% in pilot customers; increase adoption of saved trace queries by 40%; no regressions in Console page load time (> 100ms added).
acceptance_criteria: A unified query panel exists at the top of the trace workspace allowing combination of filters (time range, model, route, latency bucket, correlation ID) and free-text search
Timeline supports span stacking, lane grouping by service, and hover-to-highlight correlated spans across requests
Request detail canvas opens as a detachable drawer and shows: span list, raw request/response, correlation breadcrumbs, and quick links to related requests
Keyboard shortcuts: '/' focuses query input, 'Enter' runs query, 'J/K' navigate results, 'D' toggles detail drawer
Saved queries can be created, renamed, and applied; saved query usage metrics emit telemetry events
Design tokens and spacing conform to Console style; accessible color contrast and screen-reader labels exist for critical controls

decisions: Keep query state in the URL to allow deep linking and sharing of investigations
Implement detached detail canvas (drawer) rather than modal to preserve context and timeline visibility
Expose limited raw payloads by default; require privilege to view full payloads (tie to RBAC) - security constraint noted for PM/ENG
Telemetry will be sampled for high-cardinality events (ENG to propose sampling rate)
open_questions: How should we represent aggregated spans from batched requests? (UI: virtualized merge vs. show separate lanes)
What is the canonical correlation ID key names across model runtimes? Need mapping table from infra team
Do we provide a compact mobile layout for on-call viewing or restrict this pattern to desktop?
Should saved queries support parameterized templates (e.g., $ENV, $ROUTE) for reuse across teams?
